previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on dialysis, and a history of recurrent infections was admitted for persistent urinary incontinence and suprapubic fullness following a recent UTI. She was found to have leukocytosis and a positive urine culture growing multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae. Empiric IV meropenem was started and continued post-hemodialysis. A renal ultrasound showed a distended bladder with sediment and mild wall thickening, confirming urinary retention. She was restarted on daily straight catheterizations. Due to concerns about antibiotic access at her dialysis center and pending fosfomycin sensitivity results, she elected early discharge with a plan to follow up with her PCP. She was discharged on home health services for catheterization and IV antibiotic coordination.
